correctness.rationale: Exact disjoint alternating-cycle counting yields joint falling-factorial moments for arbitrary parameter strata. The root-size ratio w(k+1)/w(k) concentrates each root set at n/log n; hypergeometric overlap gives survival q with -log q times log n tending to two. Mixed factorial moments, upper-tail domination, and a Laplace-transform calculation prove the point-process, max-cycle and exponential mass laws. Direct enumeration of every pair through n=5 checks finite identities, but infinity follows from analytic proof.

Prior commuting-idempotent formulas condition on commutation, which fails with high probability here. Exact moments are derived anew for the present model.

originality.rationale: The unabsorbed bipartite component Poisson–Dirichlet law of Hansen–Jaworski and classical random-map/idempotent counts do not imply the exact killed alternating-cycle factorial moments or logarithmic Poisson point spectrum for a composition of independent uniform retractions. The closest indexed findings concern a single retraction, unrestricted maps, mutually annihilating pairs, or commuting pairs; no statement with the same hypotheses and consequence was located. Priority remains qualified by unlocated general killed mapping theorems.
residual_risks: A general theorem for cycles in bipartite random maps with absorbing/killed vertices might subsume the conditional moment or Poisson limit even though not identified by searches.
The full text of the Dalal–Schmutz article was inspected in its open-access parsed form, but an independent page-image view was temporarily unavailable.
The origin of every general root-enumeration theorem was not comprehensively traced; the classical root-count formula is not claimed as new.

value.rationale: Products of acyclic nonidentity retractions can create nontrivial cycles. The result identifies a natural logarithmic cycle-length scale created by absorbing overlap and a precise intensity e^(-2t)dt/t, not explained by the classical macroscopic bipartite mapping law. Exact parameter-conditioned moments, a Poisson spectrum, an extremal distribution and an exponential total mass provide reusable structural insight into random finite transformation products.
